newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO'S KOUBA SET FOR LOAN TO KAISERSLAUTERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO'S KOUBA SET FOR LOAN TO KAISERSLAUTERN.

text.p: Czech international goalkeeper Petr Kouba is set to be loaned to Germany's Kaiserslautern by his current squad Deportivo Coruna for next season, Kouba's agent said on Tuesday.
Kouba, who joined Deportivo last July after shooting to prominence with his Euro 96 performance, has seen his way to a regular place barred by the acrobatic Jacques Songo'o.
He has appeared only when Songo'o is on international duty with Cameroon and after playing just one Cup and two league games, Kouba has openly expressed his dissatisfaction.

"The president of the Spanish club (Deportivo) will in no case sell Petr, but he is prepared to allow him to play as a guest (for Kaiserslautern) next year," Kouba's agent Pavel Paska told the daily Pravo.
Kouba would join compatriots Pavel Kuka and Miroslav Kadlec at Kaiserslautern, German champions in 1991, who last month bounced back to the first division after just one season in the second.
"Petr has already received an offer from Kaiserslautern and there will be meetings between the two clubs. The offer Petr has received will have to be considered," he added.

Kouba helped the unfancied Czechs reach the Euro 96 final at Wembley in which they were beaten 2-1 by the Germans, the "golden goal" winner from Oliver Bierhoff slipping through his hands in sudden-death extra-time.
